title: Cannot escape out of the search sidebar anymore
body:
Issue Type: Bug I want the Escape key to close the sidebar if it's open. Long ago (January 2018?) I added this shortcut key to do this: ``` { "key": "escape", "command": "workbench.action.toggleSidebarVisibility", "when": "sidebarVisible" } ``` It worked great... for a while. As of today, this shortcut no longer works. I believe it's been broken since the Fall 2018 release. I don't care about this specific shortcut... I just want to be able to close the sidebar with the Escape key. How can I do that? UPDATE: The sidebar I'm mostly trying to escape from is the Search sidebar, not the workspace explorer sidebar. This used to work and now it doesn't. UPDATE 2: the problem is that the `"sidebarVisible"` context was renamed to `"sideBarVisible"`. using the new name fixes the problem. but seriously vscode team, why rename something like this? VS Code version: Code - Insiders 1.36.0-insider (fe0c3e785c22c3ed2d5caa7178488c92d62bdb08, 2019-06-28T12:34:35.956Z) OS version: Windows_NT x64 10.0.17763

author: bruceoberg

comments.body:
It works for me.
Just if the focus is in the tree, the first escape will clear the focus. And only the second escape will execute your command.
This happens because the tree is eating up the first escape key and this can not be customisable.
Thus forwarding this issue to @joaomoreno though I think we can close this as designed.

@bruceoberg I suggest that you simply use a different shortcut which is not already taken by the tree.
i am most concerned with the search sidebar, not the explorer sidebar/tree control. my shortcut used to work there and does not anymore.
We can (maybe) make <kbd>Escape</kbd> a contributable tree command instead of hardcoding it.
please remember that this is about escaping from the search sidebar, not from the workspace explorer.

# Reproduce the problem
Tried to Check if the Search sidebar looses focus on `escape` keypress.

- [x] Can confirm the focus retains in the search bar ever after multiple keypresses.

# Problem 
The problem is with how you have written the json file as the toggle doesn't require a when condition and hence removing it should fix the problem

# Solutiion
The new json looks like this and works. 
```json
{
    "key": "escape",
    "command": "workbench.action.toggleSidebarVisibility",
}
```

# Feedback
Please tell if this fixes your problem!

the `"when": "sidebarVisible"` clause is necessary because i don't want escape to reopen the sidebar if it is not open. i want escape with no sidebar to do nothing. there does not appear to be a "hideSidebar" command that does not toggle. this used to work and was broken.

and... the real problem is that `"sidebarVisible"` was renamed to `"sideBarVisible"` (note the capital B). the predicate names are case sensitive, and thus my shortcut was broken. with the new spelling it works again.

hey vscode team... don't rename `"when"` predicates!

Sorry about that!
Yes we renamed it, ti was mentioned in the release notes (I believe)

@isidorn, this is a classic case of why it is a very bad idea to rename things in passive environments (where misnamed items fail silently). you believe it was mentioned in the release notes. this is simply not good enough for a widely used product. the thing is, when my shortcut stopped working, _i did not know why_. to find out why, i had to troubleshoot it, ask for help, waste others time, and then finally stumble upon what had actually happened. all because someone thought one lower case b should be capitalized. i'm glad you're sorry about that. in the future, the vscode team should try to avoid making changes that silently break things.

For anyone coming across this, this is the full keybinding (add to your `keybindings.json`) that will close the sidebar when pressing escape:
```json
{
    "key": "escape",
    "command": "workbench.action.toggleSidebarVisibility",
    "when": "sideBarVisible"
}
```

title: Ctrl-C kills VSCode if started from command prompt
body:
- VSCode Version: 1.9.1
- OS Version: Windows 10 Anniversary Update

Steps to Reproduce:

1. From the command prompt, run "C:\Program Files (x86)\Microsoft VS Code\Code.exe". 
2. Press Ctrl-C from command prompt, VSCode exits immediately
author: wm1

comments.body: This is as expected.

Why such a behavior is expected? A child process (at least on Windows) started from cmd.exe is not supposed to be killed when the parent process receives a Ctrl-C.

I work from command line all the time, and start Code there. Ctrl-C killing the editor is not a great experience for me.
What should Ctrl C do, then?

Code.exe **is** a child console process. That's just how Chromium works.

If you don't want that, I suggest to use what we put in the `PATH`: simply type `code`. It should point to `...\Microsoft VS Code\bin\code.cmd`. This will get you a detached Code.

Before replying last time I did check that code.exe is a gui process:

`link.exe /dump /headers "C:\Program Files (x86)\Microsoft VS Code\Code.exe" | findstr subsystem
               2 subsystem (Windows `**GUI**`)`

Anyhow, code.cmd solves my problem. And I guess that is why nobody complains about this issue. I was not aware of this script as I never allow programs to update PATH.

In the meantime, I figure out that "start **/b** <path-to-code.exe>" also works, which basically sets CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP and thus the new process won't receive Ctrl-C targeting the original group.

title: Git integration fails to see merged file as staged if I reject all incoming edits
body:
VS Code Version 1.2.1
Commit fe7f407b95b7f78405846188259504b34ef72761
Date 2016-06-14T13:00:22.146Z
Shell 0.37.6
Renderer 49.0.2623.75
Node 5.10.0
Windows 10 Enterprise x64, latest non-Insider
git version 2.9.0.windows.1

Description: during a Git merge process, VSCode can sometimes show no pending changes and refuse to let me commit, while command-line Git believes a merge is in progress and lets me commit. This occurs if the changed file contains no changes (after merge) that came from the commit that I am merging into my local state.

Steps to Reproduce:
1. Create Git repository (e.g. on GitHub).
2. Clone to working folder A.
3. In working folder A, commit a file with some arbitrary text. Commit and sync
4. Clone to working folder B.
5. In working folder B, change some part of the file. Commit and sync.
6. In working folder A, change some part of the file, conflicting with previous. Commit and sync.

This will result in a merge conflict due to the change from working folder B getting pulled.

Resolve the conflict by removing all changes pulled form working folder B - the file should be the same as the committed state that existed in working folder A. Stage the file to mark the file as resolved.

Expected result: file is staged and VSCode lets you commit the merge.

Actual result: file disappears from Git tab and VSCode says cannot commit as there are no pending changes.

`git commit` from the command line works fine to finish the merge, only VSCode refuses to cooperate here.
author: sandersaares

comments.body:
This is a bit unfortunate and a not so common real world case. It happens when:
- There are no changes other than conflicting changes
- The conflict resolution for **all** changes is to take `A` version

The command line `git` will create an _empty_ commit, since there is nothing to be done on the merge commit. Code will just not let you do a commit since it doesn't support empty commits.

We should maybe make Code aware that a merge is in progress, thus allowing the completion of the merge to follow.
Related to #6403. Fix could be done regarding both.
Any update here?
#88034 is probably a duplicate.

I also recently came across this. I think it's not necessarily a rare thing for beginners who are experimenting with a simple repo and simple conflicts. It is very confusing with the way this just disappears in the UI even though the merge isn't complete. 

A fix would be very helpful.
Fixed by adding an action to `Create Empty Commit` to the notification

@joaomoreno this totally works and is clearly a corner case, but its not the most intuitive notification. i wish I could see that I did something with the merge conflicts and create empty commit changes to something like "ignore all incoming merge conflicts". i imagine anything more custom is not trivial so I do not reopen this.
